overtaking.text: DRS is gone for 2026. Active aero gives Straight Mode: in FIA-defined zones any driver can flatten the front and rear wing flaps to cut drag, with no gap-to-car-ahead requirement. The flaps close when the driver brakes, lifts or closes them manually, and some zones have cut-offs so the wings stay shut through certain corners. Overtake Mode is the actual passing aid: a driver within one second of the car ahead at a detection point (normally near the final corner) gets an extra 0.5 MJ of energy and a stronger deployment profile on the next lap. The car ahead's deployment tapers above roughly 290 km/h, while the chasing car can run full 350 kW up to about 337 km/h. Drivers can also press a Boost button anywhere on the lap to deploy stored energy. Zone counts vary by track, from none at Monaco to five at Albert Park and Spa. [1][2][3]

circuits.character: A temporary track on the park roads around Albert Park Lake. It is bumpy and slippery at the start of the weekend, then grips up as rubber goes down. It is one of the quicker laps of the year, flowing through fast lakeside sweeps, and it rewards a stable chassis with a responsive front end.
circuits.overtaking: Formula1.com names the opening chicane as the main place for wheel-to-wheel battles. The FIA set five Straight Mode zones for 2026: the pit straight, Turns 2-3, Turns 5-6, Lakeside Drive (Turns 8-9) and the run down to Turn 11. Overtake Mode detection is just after Turn 13, with activation before the final corner, Turn 14.

circuits.character: Built on former marshland, with a layout meant to echo the Chinese character shang (upwards). The lap opens with a fast entry into Turns 1-2 that wraps sharply left through Turns 3-4. Turns 7-8 bring some of the highest lateral loads of the season, and the back straight between Turns 13 and 14 runs for about 1.2 km.
circuits.overtaking: The Turn 14 hairpin at the end of the long back straight is the main passing spot. Turn 6 is the other recognised place to pass.

circuits.character: A figure-eight drivers' circuit that rewards commitment. The S Curves in the first sector demand rhythm and downforce, the two Degner corners punish hesitation, and the flat-out 130R is one of the bravest corners in F1.
circuits.overtaking: Formula1.com does not name passing zones. It flags the Hairpin as a magnet for incidents. Flowing, high-commitment layouts like this are generally hard to pass on.

circuits.character: A temporary layout around the Hard Rock Stadium complex. It feels like a street track but runs largely on private land. Three long straights take cars past 350 km/h. The Turns 13-16 section climbs over an exit ramp and dives under flyovers, through a cramped uphill chicane at Turns 14-15.
circuits.overtaking: Formula1.com points to Turns 1, 11 and 17 as the best places to see passes; each sits at the end of a long straight. Race start was brought forward three hours (from 4pm to 1pm ET) because of a storm threat.

circuits.character: A fast, low-downforce, stop-start lap. Quick straights are linked by heavy-braking chicanes and a hairpin that is hard on brakes. The lap ends at the final chicane beside the Wall of Champions, named after Hill, Villeneuve and Schumacher all hit it in 1999. In 2026 it moved to a May date and hosted its first Sprint.
circuits.overtaking: The hairpin is the classic passing spot; Formula1.com recommends Grandstands 15, 21 and 24 around it for watching moves.

circuits.character: The narrowest and slowest lap of the year, run between barriers through the principality. It is all about precision: the Swimming Pool chicane is taken at around 200 km/h, and Casino Square is the postcard view. The smallest error ends a race, and qualifying usually decides the result.
circuits.overtaking: Passing is close to impossible; the 2003 race had none. For 2026 the FIA set no Straight Mode zone, the first race weekend without movable wings since DRS arrived in 2011. Overtake Mode is still available: detection is between the Swimming Pool and Rascasse, with activation just before Turns 18-19. Red Bull's season guide notes that two mandatory pit stops add strategic jeopardy.

circuits.character: A long-time testing venue that mixes high- and low-speed corners. Teams know it well enough that it shows clearly where each car stands. The long right-hander at Turn 3 is the best test of a car's balance. In 2026 Barcelona runs under its own name because Madrid now hosts the Spanish Grand Prix.
circuits.overtaking: The braking zone into Turn 1, at the end of the long main straight, is the best passing spot; Grandstand A overlooks it.

circuits.character: A short lap that packs in a lot. The first half is about power: three straights broken by two uphill right-handers. The second half drops downhill through quick corners, including the Rindt right-hander, like a toboggan run through the Styrian hills.
circuits.overtaking: Formula1.com does not name passing zones. The braking zones after the three first-half straights, into the uphill right-handers, are where speed differences show.

circuits.character: One of the fastest tracks on the calendar and host of the first world championship race. The layout has changed many times but kept its character. The Maggotts-Becketts sequence and the flat-out Abbey are among the toughest corners of the year, and high-speed balance matters more than traction.
circuits.overtaking: Formula1.com names the Stowe area as one of the best passing spots. Pirelli brought its hardest trio for 2026.

circuits.character: The longest lap on the calendar, a drivers' favourite of long straights and fast corners through the Ardennes forest. The Eau Rouge-Raidillon climb is the most famous corner sequence in racing. The track is so long that one part can be wet while another is dry, so grip can change from corner to corner.
circuits.overtaking: Formula1.com does not name passing zones; the long full-throttle stretches are where cars get close enough to attack. Spa had five Straight Mode zones in 2026, the season maximum.

circuits.character: A twisty, karting-style lap of linked corners and short straights. Teams run Monaco-level downforce, and a well-sorted chassis matters more than engine power. Drivers enjoy finding the rhythm; Red Bull's guide calls it Monaco without the barriers.
circuits.overtaking: Formula1.com does not name passing zones, and passing is hard on this layout. Its most famous move was historic: Piquet around the outside of Senna to win in 1986.

circuits.character: A fast, undulating, old-school track that rolls through the sand dunes like a rollercoaster. It was modernised for F1's 2021 return with steep banking at the Hugenholtzbocht and at the final corner, Arie Luyendijkbocht. Red Bull's guide lists 2026 as the final Dutch Grand Prix.
circuits.overtaking: The FIA set only two Straight Mode zones: the pit straight, and the run from Turn 10 to the Turns 11-12 chicane. Active aero is not allowed through the banked final corner, but drivers can trigger Overtake Mode on the banking ahead of the pit straight. Tarzan (Turn 1) is the natural attack point; Formula1.com recommends it to spectators.

circuits.character: The Temple of Speed, in a wooded royal park north-east of Milan, where cars are at full throttle for about 80% of the lap. Low-drag top speed on the 1.1 km main straight is traded against stability under braking for the chicanes. Key corners are the Variante Ascari and the long Parabolica (Curva Alboreto), and the old banking is still visible.
circuits.overtaking: The first chicane, the Variante del Rettifilo, is the prime passing spot and the site of most first-lap battles; cars brake there from about 350 to 70 km/h. There are four Straight Mode zones: the main straight, Curva Grande to the second chicane, Lesmo 2 to Ascari, and the run to Parabolica. Overtake Mode is detected just before Parabolica and activated on its exit.

circuits.character: New for 2026: a hybrid layout around the IFEMA exhibition grounds and Valdebebas, mixing public roads with purpose-built sections, and F1's first new venue since Las Vegas in 2023. Its signature is La Monumental, Turn 12: a semicircular banked curve about 550 m long with gradients up to 24%, watched by around 45,000 fans. Turn 8 is a heavy stop into a blind apex over a crest, and the walled final sector ends in a tight last corner onto the pit straight.
circuits.overtaking: There are two Straight Mode zones: the start-finish straight, and the long straight after Turn 3. Active aero is banned in sectors two and three, including La Monumental. Overtake Mode is detected just before Turn 22 and activated on its exit, onto the main straight. La Monumental allows several lines, and Turn 8 is a big braking zone.

circuits.character: A street circuit of two halves. A huge flat-out run along the Caspian seafront contrasts with a cramped climb through the medieval old town past the Icheri Sheher walls. Teams must trade downforce for the twisty section against low drag for the straight, and as in Monaco, small mistakes end in the wall. In 2026 the race ran on a Saturday.
circuits.overtaking: Most passing happens into the 90-degree Turn 1 at the end of the main straight, where cars brake from about 350 km/h. Slipstreaming is strong enough that cars can arrive three abreast.

circuits.character: F1's stand-in for the cancelled Bahrain race, and its first visit to Sepang since 2017. The track is wide and complete: long straights, heavy stops and fast flowing corners such as the Turns 5-6 sweep. Heat, humidity and sudden tropical storms make it unpredictable. The race ran in daylight at 3pm local, not Bahrain's usual night slot, and teams arrived with no data from current-generation cars.
circuits.overtaking: There were four Straight Mode zones: the pit straight into Turn 1, Turn 3 to Turn 4, Turns 8-9, and the back straight to the Turn 15 hairpin. The final hairpin invites late-braking moves, and the width of the track gives attackers several lines.

circuits.character: A night race on a bumpy street track under the Singapore skyline, and one of the hardest races physically; drivers can lose up to 3 kg in the heat and humidity. A 2023 layout change cut the corner count from 23 to 19 and made the lap quicker, but it is still a long, wall-lined grind with constant steering work.
circuits.overtaking: Formula1.com does not name passing zones. Its 2026 race video highlights Verstappen's decisive move at Turn 1, the hard stop at the end of the pit straight, which is the main attack point.

circuits.character: A modern Tilke/HKS design that borrows from the classics. A steep climb leads to a wide, blind Turn 1. The esses at Turns 3-6 echo Silverstone's Maggotts-Becketts and Suzuka's S Curves, and the stadium section at Turns 12-15 nods to Hockenheim. The surface is notoriously bumpy, and the lap tests every part of a car.
circuits.overtaking: Most passes happen into Turn 1, where the uphill approach and very wide entry allow different lines. The long back straight sets up the other big chance into Turn 12. A preview referred to two Straight Mode zones.

circuits.character: At more than 2 km above sea level, the thin air cuts downforce and cooling, so cars run high-downforce wing settings yet still hit huge speeds on the long main straight. The 1959 layout survives in outline. The famous banked Peraltada is now bypassed, and the lap instead threads through a former baseball stadium packed with fans.
circuits.overtaking: The long run from the grid to Turn 1 makes it the main place to pass, at the start and later in the race. A dive into Turn 12, at the stadium section, is the riskier option. In 2025 the DRS zones were the pit straight, the exit of the Turns 2-3 complex and the exit of Turns 10-11.

circuits.character: A short, bowl-shaped, anticlockwise lap with banked corners left over from its pre-war design; it once doubled as an oval. Cars plunge through the Senna S after the start, wind through an infield of tricky camber changes, then climb the hill to a banked final turn and a long uphill drag to the line. Sudden rain often adds chaos.
circuits.overtaking: Turn 1 and the Senna S, at the end of the long uphill run from the final corner, are where most passes happen; Formula1.com calls Grandstand M above it the best spot to watch overtakes. Pirelli went a step softer than in 2025 to open up strategy.

circuits.character: A Saturday-night street race past Caesars Palace, the Bellagio and the Venetian, with an average speed close to Monza's. The surface is bumpy and low-grip and the November nights are cool, so getting tyres into their working window is the main challenge. Las Vegas also hosted the Caesars Palace Grand Prix in 1981-82, on a different layout.
circuits.overtaking: Formula1.com expects plenty of overtaking but does not name zones. The long full-throttle stretches, including the run up the Strip, are where slipstream and Overtake Mode should count most.

circuits.character: Built mainly for motorcycle racing, the lap is a fast, flowing chain of medium- and high-speed corners with few hard stops. Long, loaded corners plus desert heat put heavy strain on tyres and drivers. The race starts in the evening under lights. F1 said in mid-2026 that the event was confirmed and sold out despite regional tensions, with a European fallback (Imola was reported) prepared.
circuits.overtaking: The main straight, more than a kilometre long, feeds Turn 1 and gives the clearest chance to pass.

circuits.character: The season finale on Yas Island, a Tilke design reworked before the 2021 race to be faster and more raceable. The lap is built around one long straight with slow corners at each end. It also features the newly banked Turn 9 and a tricky Turns 10-12 section where drivers brake while still turning hard. The race starts in late afternoon and finishes under lights.
circuits.overtaking: The roughly 1.2 km straight from Turn 5 to Turn 6 is the main passing zone; Formula1.com points spectators to the West Grandstand for moves into Turn 6.
